overall: The AG found the Monson Select Board violated the Open Meeting Law by posting an insufficiently specific notice for its September 12 meeting, ordering future compliance and no further action since the votes were rescinded.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Sept. 12 notice was too vague: it did not flag a discussion of moving the fire department to the House of Art or demolishing it.
allegations.key_passage: The discussion item “Temporary Housing Fire Department Renovation – Chief Harris and Director Larivee” did not provide sufficient notice that the Board would discuss relocation of the fire department to the House of Art or demolition of the House of Art.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law's requirements.
No further action, because the Board rescinded the September 12 votes at its October 10 meeting.
remedy_passage: We order immediate and future compliance with the law’s requirements.
note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
